Hi Emily —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear scope. Attached is a consolidated response pack: a filled version of your spreadsheet plus a short network diagram and an excerpt from our operator runbook that addresses the keystore/workflow questions. Highlights:

- Deployment modes: Redwood supports three private patterns — managed VPC with customer peering, customer VPC with our private-control-plane connectors, and fully offline (air-gap) installs. The attached matrix maps feature differences and operational trade-offs.
- Operator access: we use role-based operator identities with ephemeral certs backed by the customer's KMS/HSM for on-prem installs. For air-gapped sites we provide signed operator credentials and a verifiable operator-handshake utility — see runbook excerpt.
- Patching: offline updates are delivered as signed artifacts (SHA256 + RSA sig). Customers validate signatures via our verification helper; we publish SBOMs and a deterministic upgrade checklist.
- Telemetry: runtime telemetry can be routed to a customer-owned collector (Fluentd/Graylog) and retention is fully configurable. Minimal heartbeat metrics may be required for service health but can be downgraded to an SMS/console-only channel if policy demands.

Two quick questions where we'd appreciate clarification before finalizing:
1) For air-gapped environments, does Orbis require a signed attest artifact from the installer after operator onboarding?
2) Are you able to share the exact retention window that procurement/security expect for telemetry (days/weeks)?

I'll loop Karhtik (technical lead) in my next note for deeper product nuance — he can provide kernel/quantization constraints and expected throughput baselines for the models you listed.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Orbis's questionnaire and our initial answers. Emily asked good clarifying questions (see my two bullets below). Can you please help with the two areas I want to tighten in the PDF and provide short snippets we can add back into the runbook excerpt?

1) Kernel/sequence-length constraints: Orbis listed two model families (Llama-XXL-ish and a proprietary 8k encoder). We should call out recommended quantization and expected throughput per GPU for the 8k profile and any special attention for KV cache sizing.

2) Operator attest flow for air-gapped installs: Emily is asking if Orbis can get a signed attest artifact post-install. Vanessa, can you draft a short sequence (installer -> operator -> customer KMS -> signed attest artifact) and an example of the verification command (we can include a deterministic output snippet)?

If you can get drafts by EOD tomorrow I will send a consolidated update to Emily and the procurement team.

Thanks —
Tessa

Thanks Tessa (and team) — the attachment looks comprehensive and the network diagram is helpful. A few narrow follow-ups from our security team so we can close this stage:

1) Signed attest artifact: yes — we require a signed installation attest that proves the operator identity and exact image/SBOM hash used during installation. The artifact should be exportable to our audit bucket as a JSON envelope. Is there a standard spec you use for that envelope?

2) Telemetry retention: security requests a configurable retention floor of 90 days for operational logs that remain within our control; any longer-term analytics exports must be opt-in.

3) Operator rotation cadence: please confirm the shortest recommended operator key/cert rotation cadence for both VPC-managed and air-gapped modes.

Also attaching our internal checklist (procurement checklist.pdf) and a short transport policy doc — these may help you tailor the answers. Once we have the three bullets above clarified we can move to the formal RFP and a DocuSign for an NDA/timetable.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emily

Attachments: orbis_procurement_checklist.pdf, orbis_transport_policy.pdf
